title: AI for Corporate Communications and Marketing

questions.question: Why do AI-assisted communication drafts need explicit review controls?
options: Because AI drafts use longer sentences than the corporate style guide allows
Because campaign copy must be translated before it reaches internal channels
Because the communications team writes faster than the model does in practice
Because polished text can hide weak sources, tone risk, or missing approval
questions.explanation: Review controls protect source quality, tone, claims, and approval ownership. Tone quality is not the same as factual reliability.

questions.question: Before AI-assisted copy is used, which four things does this lesson say to check?
options: The audience, the claim being made, the sensitivity of the topic, and the owner
The headline length, the keyword density, the call to action, and the send time
The channel, the campaign budget, the target reach, and the expected click rate
The translation quality, the image rights, the file format, and the archive path
questions.explanation: The review gate checks audience, claim, sensitivity, and owner, and the artifact turns those four signals into a review priority. The channel plan then decides how much review is required.

questions.question: What does the Python artifact produce?
options: A ranked communications review plan with controls and rationale
A published press release routed to the agreed external channels
A social media schedule built from the approved campaign messages
A translation of the approved copy into each market's local language
questions.explanation: The artifact ranks scenarios and recommends review controls. Publishing stays a human decision with a named owner.

questions.question: Which control belongs to this lesson?
options: A tone check skipped when the draft already matches the house style
A named approval owner who signs off before a sensitive message goes out
A source pack assembled after publication, in case questions come back
A channel plan chosen by whoever happens to publish the message first
questions.explanation: A named approval owner is a key communications control, and sensitive messages need one. The source pack, tone check, and channel plan are the others this lesson teaches.

questions.question: When should AI-assisted communication require stronger review?
options: Only when the draft is longer than the channel's usual published format allows
Only when the campaign runs in more than one language across several markets
When the message has external reach, sensitive content, a brand claim, or an approval gap
Only when the message will be published rather than sent to a mailing list
questions.explanation: Risk signals decide how much review is needed: audience risk, brand claim, sensitive topic, and approval gap.

questions.question: What should AI improve in communications work?
options: Drafting speed, together with source, tone, and approval discipline
The number of channels a single message can be published across
The turnaround time, by publishing before the approval owner replies
The consistency of house style, so the tone check becomes unnecessary
questions.explanation: AI should support quality and review discipline, not bypass it. Speed is only useful alongside source, tone, and approval checks.
